candidates.statement: In general, FDA’s guidance documents do not establish legally enforceable responsibilities. 140 Instead, guidances describe the Agency’s current thinking on a topic and should be viewed only 141 as recommendations, unless specific regulatory or statutory requirements are cited. The use of 142 the word should in Agency guidances means that something is suggested or recommended, but 143 not required. 144

candidates.statement: A. Components of a PCCP 378 A PCCP should consist of a detailed Description of Modifications, a Modification Protocol, and 379 an Impact Assessment (see Section VII. of this guidance) because these components are intended 380 to provide FDA with information that will enable our review of the proposed modifications. The 381 detailed Description of Modifications should outline the specific, planned modifications that may 382 be made to the device. This includes defining the specifications for the characteristics and 383 performance of the planned modifications to the device. The Modification Protocol should 384 describe the verification and validation activities, including pre-defined acceptance criteria, that 385 will support each modification to assure the device remains safe and effective across the intended 386 use populations. The Impact Assessment helps to tie the Description of Modifications to the 387 Modification Protocol in that the Impact Assessment identifies the benefits and risks introduced 388 by the specified, planned modifications and addresses how the verification and validation 389 activities of the Modification Protocol will continue to assure the safety and effectiveness of the 390 device. The detailed Description of Modifications, Modification Protocol, and Impact 391 Assessment are all interrelated components of a PCCP. 392

candidates.statement: For devices subject to 510(k) requirements, the determination of substantial equivalence 453 includes, among other requirements, a comparison between the technological characteristics of 454 the predicate device and the subject device. 46 In FDA’s determination of substantial equivalence, 455 FDA considers the PCCP to be part of the technological characteristics of the device. For 510(k) 456 submissions, in making a determination of substantial equivalence where the predicate device 457 was authorized with a PCCP, the subject device must be compared to the version of the predicate 458 device cleared or approved prior to changes made under the PCCP. 47 Once a 510(k) for a device 459 that includes modifications that have been implemented consistent with the authorized PCCP has 460 been cleared in a subsequent marketing submission, such device can now serve as an eligible 461 predicate device. The PCCP can be considered during the 510(k) review process at multiple 462 points in the decision tree to address the critical questions in the 510(k) Decision-Making 463 Flowchart. 48 In general, FDA anticipates that the PCCP will primarily be reviewed after FDA 464 finds that the intended use of the subject device and the predicate device are the same, to help 465 determine whether the devices have different technological characteristics that do not raise 466 different questions of safety and effectiveness. 49

candidates.statement: 1119 Please note that the provided summaries of the devices and modifications in this section are not how the individual modifications included in the PCCP impact not only the particular device function, but the overall functionality of the device, including how they impact other device software functions and/or device hardware. For combination products, such documentation should also discuss how the individual modifications included in the PCCP for the device constituent part impact the biologic and/or drug constituent part, and the combination product as a whole. Additionally, if the modifications in a PCCP are intended to affect any device functions of a multiple function device product, we recommend considering FDA’s guidance “Multiple Function Device Products: Policy and Considerations. ” In particular, as it pertains to the device and the PCCP, it is important to determine if any information should be included in the Impact Assessment in a PCCP in a marketing submission so that FDA may assess the impact of the “other function(s)” on the safety or effectiveness of the device as it is modified consistent with Some information related to the Impact Assessment may be included elsewhere in your marketing submission, for example in sections for the risk assessment for the device or the Modification Protocol in your PCCP. As such, FDA recommends providing clear references in your Impact Assessment to the relevant sections in your marketing submission that support the Impact Assessment.
